summary: This benchmark evaluates whether compartmentalizing autoregressive language models with hard connectivity boundaries ('walls' and 'doors') induces domain selectivity and enables modular module transplantation. Across 400M-token runs on a multilingual/code mix, neither walled compartments, brain-inspired wiring penalties, nor mixture-of-experts baselines developed significant domain selectivity, yielding a well-documented null result with thorough ablation and recovery metrics.
strengths: Preregistered evaluation methodology with explicit quantitative thresholds for selectivity and recovery, resisting publication bias through transparent reporting of null findings.
Careful experimental controls, including equal token budgets, identical batch compositions across arms, and isolating door refitting from room transplantation.
Complete internal arithmetic consistency across reported FLOPs, relative loss increases, and damage recovery percentages.
Comprehensive documentation of hardware configuration, library versions, random seeds, wall-clock runtimes, and training hyperparameters.
weaknesses: The 400M-token pretraining budget for ~100M–150M parameter decoders is significantly undertrained relative to compute-optimal scaling, leaving open whether domain specialization emerges at higher data-to-parameter ratios.
Evaluation is restricted to three pretraining domains (English, Python, Welsh) and a single donor-recipient seed pair for module transplantation.
Lack of confidence intervals or variance estimates across multiple runs due to single-seed serial training.
suggestions: Scale training tokens to compute-optimal regimes (e.g., 2B+ tokens for 100M parameter models) to assess whether specialization requires saturation.
Test modular transplantation across additional donor-recipient seed pairs and varying channel bottleneck widths to establish statistical error margins.
Evaluate task-specific downstream benchmarks in addition to cross-entropy validation loss.

claims.text: TopoLM uses a spatial smoothness objective on activations.
The circular wiring-length penalty tested here follows a different choice closer to brain-inspired modular training.
A transplanted room followed by door refitting recovered 67.0% of the code-loss damage, slightly above 64.3% for door refitting with the room still removed.
claims.source: Internal arithmetic verification: intact code loss 1.852, removed 2.469 (damage = 0.617); transplant refit 2.056 (recovery = (2.469-2.056)/0.617 = 66.94%); removed refit 2.072 (recovery = (2.469-2.072)/0.617 = 64.34%).

claims.text: Training the new room alone recovered 86.1% of full fine-tuning's Icelandic gain with smaller loss increases on each old domain.
claims.source: Internal arithmetic verification: new room Icelandic gain = 2.140, full fine-tuning gain = 2.486; ratio = 2.140 / 2.486 = 86.08%.

novelty_vs_existing.title: TopoLM: brain-like spatio-functional organization in a topographic language model
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While TopoLM enforces spatial smoothness over continuous activation maps to emulate cortical topography, this submission evaluates discrete structural modularity ('rooms' separated by shared bottleneck channels) and biological wiring-length penalties directly for domain specialization and weight transplantability.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Seeing is Believing: Brain-Inspired Modular Training for Mechanistic Interpretability
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: BIMT demonstrated modular self-organization on toy symbolic and algorithmic tasks via connection length penalties; this benchmark applies wiring penalties and explicit architectural walls to 100M-scale autoregressive language models trained on mixed multilingual and code text.
